reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line of the chapter was read against the Greek. No line adds interpretive content, uses Raëlian-canon vocabulary (no Elohim, Yahweh, craft, creators, ray, planet, Eternals), or resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own paragraph headed 'reception note, not a translation claim'. The two lines that coincide with the canon's French were tested specifically: 2:2/2:9 'at its rising' (BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB 1970, NRSV, ESV) and 26:53 'put at my disposal' (BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites the verse; NASB identical wording). In both the lexical ground is real and independent of the canon, so neither is lens leakage.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed from the Greek, the chapter JSON, the overlay and the central diff before the escalation report (wave-m2-editor-report.md) was opened. The report added no information that changes a verdict. It repeats the RSV attribution for 2:2/9 ('RSV, NRSV, NAB'), which this review corrects. Its ten founder-preference points are answered in founderDecisionRecommendations, and its follow-ups (17:21; 17:22; comma/colon in 25 and 28; the 6:13 'testing' wording in central) are endorsed as later-pass items.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-colon-convention: Endorse (punctuation only; applied without exception in the wave). Harmonize published 25 and 28 in a later pass.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-magi: Endorse. 'magi' is the standard scholarly rendering (BDAG; Brown; Powell) and NIV/NAB usage; 'wise men' is noted.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.8-at-its-rising-2:2,9: Endorse. BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB (1970, before TBWTT) and NRSV read 'at its rising', ESV 'when it rose'. Correct the RSV attribution (the RSV reads 'in the East').
founderDecisionRecommendations.9-defiles-a-person: Endorse. The article with ἄνθρωπος is generic; the canon's own French « l'homme » is generic too, so the line follows the sense the canon intends rather than the English edition's 'the man'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.10-tempted-4:1: Endorse. Agent-driven 'tempted'/'the tempter' is BDAG's and the versions' reading with the devil as agent, and agrees with published 6:13; the test reading (Gerhardsson; canon « mis à l'épreuve ») is properly in commentary. Optionally align the chapter 4 title ('The testing in the wilderness') with the line.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai embas eis ploion dieperasen kai ēlthen eis tēn idian polin.

i18n.en: And getting into a boat, he crossed over and came into his own city.

notes.official: *tēn idian polin* 'his own city': Capernaum, where Jesus settled (4:13).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον. καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Θάρσει, τέκνον· ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou prosepheron autō paralytikon epi klinēs beblēmenon. kai idōn ho iēsous tēn pistin autōn eipen tō paralytikō· tharsei, teknon· aphientai sou hai hamartiai.

i18n.en: And behold, they were bringing to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic: "Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven."

notes.official: *teknon* 'child', an affectionate address. *aphientai sou hai hamartiai* 'your sins are forgiven': a present passive, which leaves the forgiver implicit (the 'divine passive'); the scribes' charge in 9:3 assumes that Jesus is claiming to forgive.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou tines tōn grammateōn eipan en heautois· houtos blasphēmei.

i18n.en: And behold, some of the scribes said within themselves: "This man is blaspheming."

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἱνατί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: kai eidōs ho iēsous tas enthymēseis autōn eipen· hinati enthymeisthe ponēra en tais kardiais hymōn;

i18n.en: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said: "Why do you think evil in your hearts?

paragraphs.text: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
paragraphs.translit: ti gar estin eukopōteron, eipein· aphientai sou hai hamartiai, ē eipein· egeire kai peripatei;

i18n.en: For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?

notes.official:
*Egeire kai peripatei* 'Rise and walk': *egeirō* is also the verb of resurrection (9:25; 27:52, 64). Quoted words embedded in a running sentence keep a comma (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 9:5 and 9:7 (« Lève-toi et marche (…) (et) il se leva ») and reads the healing of the paralytic, like that of the leper, as an operation at a distance by a concentrated ray. The canon's wording agrees with the Greek here; the line renders it lexically.

paragraphs.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: hina de eidēte hoti exousian echei ho huios tou anthrōpou epi tēs gēs aphienai hamartias— tote legei tō paralytikō· egertheis aron sou tēn klinēn kai hypage eis ton oikon sou.

i18n.en: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — then he says to the paralytic — "Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house."

notes.official: 'the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins': the first claim of *exousia* by the Son of Man in Matthew, which anticipates 28:18 'all authority' (`son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`). The interrupted sentence ('then he says to the paralytic') is the Greek's own anacoluthon.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai egertheis apēlthen eis ton oikon autou.

i18n.en: And he rose and went away to his house.

notes.official: *egertheis* 'he rose': the same verb as the command of 9:5 and 9:6 (see the reception note at 9:5).

paragraphs.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
paragraphs.translit: idontes de hoi ochloi ephobēthēsan kai edoxasan ton theon ton donta exousian toiautēn tois anthrōpois.

i18n.en: But when the crowds saw it, they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to people.

notes.official: *ton donta exousian toiautēn tois anthrōpois* 'who had given such authority to people': the generic plural is rendered 'people' (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`); the draft and the ASV had 'to men'. The plural may generalize from Jesus to the community that will exercise forgiveness (16:19; 18:18). Some witnesses read *ethaumasan* 'marveled' for *ephobēthēsan* 'were afraid'; SBLGNT reads 'were afraid'.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai paragōn ho iēsous ekeithen eiden anthrōpon kathēmenon epi to telōnion, maththaion legomenon, kai legei autō· akolouthei moi· kai anastas ēkolouthēsen autō.

i18n.en: And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and he says to him: "Follow me." And he rose and followed him.

notes.official: *Maththaion legomenon* 'a man called Matthew': Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 name the tax collector Levi. *telōnion* 'tax booth'.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto autou anakeimenou en tē oikia, kai idou polloi telōnai kai hamartōloi elthontes synanekeinto tō iēsou kai tois mathētais autou.

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as he was reclining at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes hoi pharisaioi elegon tois mathētais autou· dia ti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiei ho didaskalos hymōn;

i18n.en: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples: "Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες.
paragraphs.translit: ho de akousas eipen· ou chreian echousin hoi ischyontes iatrou alla hoi kakōs echontes.

i18n.en: But when he heard it, he said: "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill.

paragraphs.text: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.
paragraphs.translit: poreuthentes de mathete ti estin· eleos thelō kai ou thysian· ou gar ēlthon kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous.

i18n.en: But go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."

notes.official:
*Eleos thelō kai ou thysian* 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice': Hos 6:6, quoted again at 12:7. *ou gar ēlthon kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous* 'For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners'. The Byzantine text and the KJV add *eis metanoian* 'to repentance', harmonizing with Luke 5:32; it is absent from the critical text (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *dikaios* is rendered 'righteous' as in 1:19 and 10:41.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes the saying without 'to repentance' (« je ne suis pas venu appeler les justes mais les pécheurs », EN 'the just') and reads it as Jesus' mission: not to Israel, which already knew of the creators, but to spread that knowledge through the world. The canon's text agrees with the critical text; 'the just' and 'the righteous' render the same word.

paragraphs.text: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
paragraphs.translit: tote proserchontai autō hoi mathētai iōannou legontes· dia ti hēmeis kai hoi pharisaioi nēsteuomen polla, hoi de mathētai sou ou nēsteuousin;

i18n.en: Then the disciples of John come to him, saying: "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?"

notes.official: *nēsteuomen polla* 'fast often': SBLGNT prints *polla*; NA28 brackets it, and Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus omit it ('Why do we and the Pharisees fast?'). The line follows SBLGNT (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφʼ ὅσον μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος; ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois ho iēsous· mē dynantai hoi huioi tou nymphōnos penthein ephʼ hoson metʼ autōn estin ho nymphios; eleusontai de hēmerai hotan aparthē apʼ autōn ho nymphios, kai tote nēsteusousin.

i18n.en: And Jesus said to them: "Can the sons of the bridechamber mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.

notes.official: *hoi huioi tou nymphōnos* 'the sons of the bridechamber': a Semitic idiom for the bridegroom's attendants or wedding guests. It is kept literal, as Matthew's other 'sons of' idioms are (8:12; 13:38; 23:15), and the sense is given here (`hoi-huioi-tou-nymphonos-mt-9-15`). *aparthē* 'is taken away' anticipates the passion.

paragraphs.text: οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ· αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: oudeis de epiballei epiblēma rhakous agnaphou epi himatiō palaiō· airei gar to plērōma autou apo tou himatiou, kai cheiron schisma ginetai.

i18n.en: And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear is made.

paragraphs.text: οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται· ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς, καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται.
paragraphs.translit: oude ballousin oinon neon eis askous palaious· ei de mē ge, rhēgnyntai hoi askoi, kai ho oinos ekcheitai kai hoi askoi apollyntai· alla ballousin oinon neon eis askous kainous, kai amphoteroi syntērountai.

i18n.en: Neither do people put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, and the wine is poured out, and the wineskins are destroyed. But they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."

paragraphs.text: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν· ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπʼ αὐτήν, καὶ ζήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: tauta autou lalountos autois idou archōn heis elthōn prosekynei autō legōn hoti hē thygatēr mou arti eteleutēsen· alla elthōn epithes tēn cheira sou epʼ autēn, kai zēsetai.

i18n.en: While he was saying these things to them, behold, a ruler came and knelt before him, saying: "My daughter has just now died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."

notes.official: *archōn heis* 'a ruler' (Mark 5:22: Jairus, a synagogue leader). *prosekynei* 'knelt before him', the gesture of a petitioner (`proskyneo-worship-kneel-matthew`). *arti eteleutēsen* 'has just now died': in Mark 5:23 the girl is still dying, and Matthew compresses the story.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai egertheis ho iēsous ēkolouthei autō kai hoi mathētai autou.

i18n.en: And Jesus rose and followed him, and so did his disciples.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai idou gynē haimorroousa dōdeka etē proselthousa opisthen hēpsato tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou·

i18n.en: And behold, a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment;

notes.official: *tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou* 'the fringe of his garment': the tassels (*ṣîṣit*) that the Law requires on the corners of garments (Num 15:38-39; Deut 22:12); the same word at 14:36 and 23:5.

paragraphs.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ· Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: elegen gar en heautē· ean monon hapsōmai tou himatiou autou sōthēsomai.

i18n.en: for she was saying within herself: "If I only touch his garment, I shall be made well."

notes.official: *sōthēsomai* 'I shall be made well': *sōzō* means both 'heal' and 'save'. The same verb is used twice in 9:22 ('has made you well', 'was made well'), so the English keeps one expression for it.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Θάρσει, θύγατερ· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous strapheis kai idōn autēn eipen· tharsei, thygater· hē pistis sou sesōken se. kai esōthē hē gynē apo tēs hōras ekeinēs.

i18n.en: But Jesus turned, and seeing her he said: "Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well." And the woman was made well from that hour.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn ho iēsous eis tēn oikian tou archontos kai idōn tous aulētas kai ton ochlon thoryboumenon

i18n.en: And when Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,

paragraphs.text: ἔλεγεν· Ἀναχωρεῖτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει· καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elegen· anachōreite, ou gar apethanen to korasion alla katheudei· kai kategelōn autou.

i18n.en: he was saying: "Go away, for the girl is not dead but is sleeping." And they were laughing at him.

notes.official: *ou gar apethanen to korasion alla katheudei* 'the girl is not dead but is sleeping': the ordinary verb for sleep (*katheudō*), not the euphemism *koimaomai* 'fall asleep' (27:52).

paragraphs.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος, εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον.
paragraphs.translit: hote de exeblēthē ho ochlos, eiselthōn ekratēsen tēs cheiros autēs, kai ēgerthē to korasion.

i18n.en: But when the crowd had been put out, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl arose.

notes.official: *ēgerthē to korasion* 'the girl arose': *egeirō*, the verb of 9:5-7 and of resurrection (27:52, 64; 28:6-7).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην.
paragraphs.translit: kai exēlthen hē phēmē hautē eis holēn tēn gēn ekeinēn.

i18n.en: And the report of this went out into all that land.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες· Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὲ Δαυίδ.
paragraphs.translit: kai paragonti ekeithen tō iēsou ēkolouthēsan autō dyo typhloi krazontes kai legontes· eleēson hēmas, huie dauid.

i18n.en: And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"

notes.official: *Huios Dauid* 'Son of David', the messianic title most often on the lips of supplicants in Matthew (15:22; 20:30-31).

paragraphs.text: ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε.
paragraphs.translit: elthonti de eis tēn oikian prosēlthon autō hoi typhloi, kai legei autois ho iēsous· pisteuete hoti dynamai touto poiēsai; legousin autō· nai, kyrie.

i18n.en: And when he had come into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus says to them: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They say to him: "Yes, Lord."

paragraphs.text: τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων· Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: tote hēpsato tōn ophthalmōn autōn legōn· kata tēn pistin hymōn genēthētō hymin.

i18n.en: Then he touched their eyes, saying: "According to your faith let it be done to you."

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί. καὶ ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēneōchthēsan autōn hoi ophthalmoi. kai enebrimēthē autois ho iēsous legōn· horate mēdeis ginōsketō·

i18n.en: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly charged them, saying: "See that no one knows it."

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de exelthontes diephēmisan auton en holē tē gē ekeinē.

i18n.en: But they went out and spread his fame in all that land.

paragraphs.text: Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον·
paragraphs.translit: autōn de exerchomenōn idou prosēnenkan autō anthrōpon kōphon daimonizomenon·

i18n.en: And as they were going out, behold, they brought to him a mute man who was demon-possessed.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekblēthentos tou daimoniou elalēsen ho kōphos. kai ethaumasan hoi ochloi legontes· oudepote ephanē houtōs en tō israēl.

i18n.en: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying: "Never has anything like this been seen in Israel."

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον· Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de pharisaioi elegon· en tō archonti tōn daimoniōn ekballei ta daimonia.

i18n.en: But the Pharisees were saying: "By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons."

notes.official: 'By the ruler of the demons': Beelzebul in 10:25 and 12:24. Codex Bezae, some Old Latin manuscripts and the Sinaitic Syriac omit the whole verse; SBLGNT and NA28 include it (Metzger, Textual Commentary, ad loc.).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai periēgen ho iēsous tas poleis pasas kai tas kōmas, didaskōn en tais synagōgais autōn kai kēryssōn to euangelion tēs basileias kai therapeuōn pasan noson kai pasan malakian.

i18n.en: And Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness.

notes.official: 'the gospel of the kingdom' (`euangelion-gospel-matthew`); the summary repeats 4:23 and closes the section framed by the two summaries.

paragraphs.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα.
paragraphs.translit: idōn de tous ochlous esplanchnisthē peri autōn hoti ēsan eskylmenoi kai errimmenoi hōsei probata mē echonta poimena.

i18n.en: And seeing the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and cast down, like sheep without a shepherd.

notes.official: *eskylmenoi kai errimmenoi* 'harassed and cast down'. *hōsei probata mē echonta poimena* 'like sheep without a shepherd': Num 27:17; 1 Kgs 22:17; Ezek 34:5.

paragraphs.text: τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι·
paragraphs.translit: tote legei tois mathētais autou· ho men therismos polys, hoi de ergatai oligoi·

i18n.en: Then he says to his disciples: "The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the workers are few;

paragraphs.text: δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: deēthēte oun tou kyriou tou therismou hopōs ekbalē ergatas eis ton therismon autou.

i18n.en: therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest."

notes.official: *tou kyriou tou therismou* 'the Lord of the harvest': *kyrios* here is the owner of the harvest within the image, and points to God.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Canon-wording check: Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει / ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν (9:5, 9:7) quoted in TBWTT ch. 4 as « Lève-toi et marche (…) (et) il se leva ». Draft 'Rise and walk' / 'he rose' agrees; ἐγείρω is the same verb used for resurrection (cf. 9:25 'the girl arose', 27:52, 27:64). No divergence expected; logged for the Editor's canon-alignment check.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: No divergence; canon wording agrees with the Greek; reception note added.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'but sinners to repentance') adds εἰς μετάνοιαν, harmonizing with Lk 5:32; absent from SBLGNT. The canon (TBWTT ch. 4) quotes « je ne suis pas venu appeler les justes mais les pécheurs » without 'to repentance', and renders δικαίους as 'the just'.
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners (critical text)
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Critical text followed; 'to repentance' recorded; 'righteous' kept (canon 'just' is the same word).

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual note: SBLGNT prints νηστεύομεν πολλά ('fast often'); NA28 brackets [πολλά], and Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus omit it.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: SBLGNT 'fast often' followed; NA28 bracket and B/א* omission recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος (hoi huioi tou nymphōnos), a Semitic idiom: literal 'the sons of the bridechamber' (ASV) vs. idiomatic 'the wedding guests' / 'the bridegroom's attendants'.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'the sons of the bridechamber' kept literal like Matthew's other 'sons of' idioms; sense given in commentary.
